lines.trans: Colette! What are you doing here?
We were taking a walk in the neighborhood.
You brought Flora with you?
Yes, she wanted to see her mother.
It is a very wonderful surprise!
I know that you work a lot.
Yes, but I miss you both so much.
Take her in your arms now.
Come with mommy, my little treasure.
She smiles at you with happiness.
You are so sweet, my Flora.
Let us take a walk in the park.
Yes, with great pleasure, Colette.
Let us take the time to pause.

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?

meanings.en: to bring (person or pet), to take along

examples.trans: Bring him to my place tonight.

meanings.en: au contraire = on the contrary; au revoir = goodbye

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

meanings.note: before the noun; bel before a vowel: un bel endroit

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

examples.text: Nous voulons le bonheur de Flora.

meanings.note: le bras droit = the right arm
être le bras droit de quelqu'un = to be someone's right hand

examples.trans: I will become his right hand.

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel
dans une heure = in an hour

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.
Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

meanings.note: pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle
before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

examples.text: Je veux, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.trans: I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Ma maman habite dans le Sud.
examples.trans: My mum lives in the South.

meanings.note: often capitalised when addressing her: Maman

meanings.en: to be missed by (tu me manques = I miss you)
meanings.note: back to front: the person missed is the subject
object pronoun before the verb: tu me donnes
with reflexive verbs: je me débrouille
everyday speech, with a he/she verb form

examples.text: Un château avec un grand parc.
examples.trans: A castle with a large park.

examples.text: Ça fait plaisir à ma famille.

meanings.en: faire plaisir à = to please, to make happy

promener.gloss: to walk (a dog), to take for a walk

meanings.note: promener son chien = walk one's dog; se promener = go for a walk

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris?

meanings.note: starts a question: qu'est-ce que tu fais? = what are you doing?

examples.trans: It is a very pleasant neighborhood.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.

meanings.en: se réunir = to meet, to convene

examples.trans: Do you know where he is?

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: je ne sais pas = I don't know

examples.text: Si tu veux le rôle, tu dois changer.
examples.trans: If you want the part, you have to change.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: J'aime le regard et le sourire.
examples.trans: I like the look and the smile.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.

meanings.note: faire la surprise à = to surprise someone
before the verb; t' before a vowel
c'est tellement stupide = it's so stupid
tout le temps = all the time
used alone, after a preposition, or for emphasis: et toi?, avec toi, toi aussi
informal, one owner; ton, ta, tes
c'est mon tour = it's my turn

examples.text: C'est mon tour d'entrer en scène.
examples.trans: It is my turn to go on stage.

meanings.note: travailler à Paris, travailler le dimanche

examples.text: Viens avec maman, mon petit trésor.
examples.trans: Come with mommy, my little treasure.

examples.text: Cette île cache un grand trésor.
examples.trans: This island hides a great treasure.

meanings.note: singular and informal: friends, family, children, colleagues of the same age
venir de: je viens de la Côte d'Azur
venir de + infinitive: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived
+ noun: je veux un café; + infinitive: je veux partir
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
